ledgerSearch.outcome: CTD-0078 requires that named scholarship not function as proof of feasibility, which governs the movement, institutional theory, and failure analysis lineages in this part. CTD-0034 tracks the Volume V encounter promise, which the invitation chapter makes and which the restoration keeps in conditional form. findings.summary: The invitation lost its three denials and its definition.

evidence.baseline: Not a call to arms. Not a manifesto. Not a claim that the people who accept will be building something that is certain to succeed or that their participation will be recognized by the world in proportion to its importance. An invitation, in the specific sense: an offer to share commitment to work that the preceding chapters have described honestly enough that the people who accept know what they are accepting.

findings.diagnosis: The three fragments are the chapter refusing three genres the reader is entitled to suspect it of, and the third denial refuses the promise of recognition, which is the most honest thing in the chapter. The card permits fragments that carry real force. Honestly enough that the people who accept know what they are accepting is also the standard the whole volume has been meeting.

findings.summary: The invitation's addressee was removed, and with it the reason it means anything.

evidence.baseline: The invitation has a specific addressee. It is not addressed to everyone. ... the invitation is most usefully accepted by people who have them rather than by people who aspire to them in the abstract. The aspiration is valuable. The work requires the reality. / The invitation is extended to the people who have read through to this chapter ... The invitation means something because the knowledge it is based on is real.

findings.authorizedBy: Compression, and catalog 4.16 read onto the address to the reader.
findings.diagnosis: 4.16 flags claims about the reader's inner state. This passage makes no such claim; it names who the invitation is for and why reading the argument is the qualification. That is the opposite of conscription, since it tells most readers the offer is not aimed at them. The aspiration and reality pair is also the chapter's only guard against self-selection by enthusiasm, which Chapter Seventeen named as a failure mode.

reasoning.note: R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Two em dashes. One introduced the specification of what an invitation is and became a colon. One was a parenthetical appositive naming the volumes and became a comma pair.
The shipped epigraph attribution Adapted from The Coherence Thesis, Volume III, required by CTD-0007.
The three denials, the definition of the invitation, the specific addressee, and the aspiration and reality pair.

openQuestions: The restored passage says the invitation is extended to people who have read through to this chapter. That is close to treating reading as a qualification, which the volume card's Direct address override bounds and which the orientation explicitly denies when it says publication is not participation. Restored under tonight's policy and flagged as a live tension between two restored passages.

The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-04 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. Catalog 4.16 fired and the retention limb held on inspection: naming who an offer is for is not the same as telling a reader what they feel. The distinction is worth carrying, because 4.16 will fire on almost every sentence in a chapter called The Invitation.
